banner.title: The systems round - Pickens' D&D Option: Weapon Damage (folio 30) and Seaton's Monkish Combat in the Arena of Promotion (folios 4-5)
banner.provenance: Pinned from The Dragon Vol. 1 No. 2 (August 1976): folio 30, Jon Pickens' Weapon Damage option - the expertise system replacing the Greyhawk damage tables, the seventeen-weapon Normal/Expert grid with the space requirements; folios 4-5, John M. Seaton's Monkish promotion combat - the DPT/DPG frame, the set-and-unit structure, the recovery doctrine, and the strike-block-kick matrix, playtested by the Missouri Mercenary Group. OD&D-era ink converted per the walk doctrine: the pin IS the conversion, noted, never silent.
banner.sentinel: The variant-layer doctrine holds: Dragon ink is never core 1e canon. The Weapon Damage option rides against the engine's canon damage tables as a noted variant, never a rewrite; the monk matrix codes are CONVERTED to integers for the grid - 0 normal DPG, 1 blocked, 2 double DPG, 3 triple DPG, 4 sweep succeeds, 5 grab, 6 not applicable - the legend pinned beside the grid, the conversion noted, never silent; the five-eighths roll of dexterity is pinned as scanned.

consts.name: sysFighterLevelsPerWeapon
consts.comment: for every THREE levels a Fighter advances he masters one additional weapon, scoring the Expert damage (folio 30)

consts.name: sysThiefLevelsPerWeapon
consts.comment: the Thief masters one weapon per FOUR levels, and only sword, dagger, a combination of these, or the sling (folio 30)

consts.name: sysThiefWeaponCount
consts.comment: the Thief's expertise list runs four: sword, dagger, the combination, the sling (folio 30)

consts.name: sysTwoWeaponDexMin
consts.comment: a Fighter or Thief with dexterity 13 or better may take a two one-handed weapon combination instead of a single expertise (folio 30)

consts.name: sysHardComboDexMin
consts.comment: Sword and Sword, or Flail and Morning Star, require dexterity 16 - especially difficult to master; only one Morning Star and/or Flail per combination (folio 30)

consts.name: sysTwoHandedStrMin
consts.comment: the 2-Handed Sword requires Strength 16 (folio 30)

consts.name: sysTwoHandedDexMin
consts.comment: the 2-Handed Sword also requires dexterity 9 (folio 30)

consts.name: sysOneHandStrMin
consts.comment: the Military Pick or Battle Axe may be wielded one-handed at Strength 16 and dexterity 9 (folio 30)

consts.name: sysOneHandDexMin
consts.comment: the one-handed pick or axe dexterity floor - 9 (folio 30)

consts.name: sysWeaponRows
consts.comment: the weapon grid runs seventeen rows, Dagger through Sling Stone (folio 30)

consts.name: sysDptLevelMult
consts.comment: Damage Points Taken = strength x constitution, plus 10 times the monk's level (folio 4)

consts.name: sysDpgIntDiv
consts.comment: Damage Points Given = strength + dexterity + half intelligence (folio 4)

consts.name: sysSetsPerTurn
consts.comment: each combat turn runs 10 sets (folio 4)

consts.name: sysUnitsPerSet
consts.comment: each set runs 6 written units of combat (folio 4)

consts.name: sysHalfStrengthPct
consts.comment: below three-quarters of his DPT, all the combatant's succeeding blows land at half strength (folio 4)

consts.name: sysHalfStrengthDiv
consts.comment: the half-strength divisor (folio 4)

consts.name: sysChangeRollNum
consts.comment: changing an order after a unit is read takes a five-eighths roll of dexterity, pinned as scanned (folio 4)

consts.name: sysChangeRollDen
consts.comment: the roll's denominator - eighths (folio 4)

consts.name: sysKickRowMax
consts.comment: up to three of the same type kicks may be used in a row (folio 4)

consts.name: sysKickHandBlocksMax
consts.comment: when kicking, the hands are used in one or two blocks (folio 4)

consts.name: sysJumpLegs
consts.comment: Jump Back and Jump Forward each move one leg length (folio 5)

consts.name: sysSweepDownUnits
consts.comment: a successful sweep puts the opponent down for three units - he gets up and cannot strike; blows struck while down do normal damage (folio 4)

consts.name: sysStampAfterSweep
consts.comment: the Stamp can be used only after a successful sweep and has no effect otherwise (folio 4) - pinned as the no-effect zero

consts.name: sysGrabUnits
consts.comment: the grab: the attacker's next three units all tell at normal value, the opponent unable to count strikes until the third unit; the blows may be blocked (folio 5)

consts.name: sysLightWoundDpt
consts.comment: recovery - for each 10 DPT lost, cure light wounds (folio 4)

consts.name: sysSeriousWoundDpt
consts.comment: for each 50 DPT lost, cure serious wounds (folio 4)

consts.name: sysWishDpt
consts.comment: for every 150 DPT lost, the combatant must be wished to health (folio 4)

consts.name: sysNaturalRecoveryDiv
consts.comment: without magic, days of recovery = DPT lost times one half (folio 4)

consts.name: sysMatrixRows
consts.comment: the matrix runs eight attack rows - Reverse Punch, Back Fist, Knife Hand, Front Kick, Head Kick, Side Kick, Sweep, Stamp (folio 5)

bools.name: sysTwoWeaponShielded
bools.comment: the two-weapon wielder strikes once with each weapon, or once with either and counts as shielded (folio 30)

bools.name: sysNoExpertiseInCombo
bools.comment: no expertise bonus while employing the two-weapon option, even if the wielder has it for either weapon (folio 30)

bools.name: sysOneFlailMorningStar
bools.comment: only one Morning Star and/or Flail may be used in a combination (folio 30)

bools.name: sysKickArmLength
bools.comment: kicks will not work within arm's length (folio 4)

bools.name: sysStrikeArmLength
bools.comment: a strike cannot connect outside arm's length - matches start at kicking distance (folio 4)

bools.name: sysStrikeFeetGrounded
bools.comment: when striking, both feet are grounded (folio 4)

bools.name: sysHandsSplit
bools.comment: except for the X-Block, both hands may attack, or one attack and one defend (folio 4)

bools.name: sysRestEachSet
bools.comment: after the initial set, at least one Rest must appear in each remaining set (folios 4-5)

bools.name: sysFirstStrikeHighDpt
bools.comment: first strike goes to the combatant with the higher DPT at the time (folio 4)

bools.name: sysReturnBlowRoll
bools.comment: a combatant killed by a first strike gets a return blow only if he beats his last DPT score on the five-eighths roll (folio 4)

bools.name: sysConcedeStops
bools.comment: a combatant may concede between blows at any time - combat stops and the victor is recognized; the advancement challenge is not to kill, though it can (folio 4)

bools.name: sysDuckHighMiddle
bools.comment: the Duck brings the body mostly below high and middle strikes and kicks (folio 5)

bools.name: sysNoChallengeWhileRecovering
bools.comment: monks will not make an advancement challenge to another while that one is recovering (folio 4)

audit_comment: THE SYSTEMS ROUND - Round D of issue 2, two systems on the variant layer. THE WEAPON DAMAGE OPTION (Pickens, folio 30): the expertise cadence - a weapon per 3 Fighter levels or 4 Thief levels, the Thief limited to sword, dagger, their combination, or the sling; the two-weapon combination at dex 13, shielded, no expertise bonus, one Flail or Morning Star at most, the hard pairs at dex 16; the 2-Handed Sword at Strength 16 and dex 9, the one-handed Pick or Battle Axe; and the seventeen-weapon grid, Dagger 1-4 / 2-5 through the Mounted Lance 2-12 / 2-24, with the space column carrying the footnotes - 4, 5 and 6 feet for the starred, the not-useable-in-dungeons length rule noted here in prose. THE MONKISH PROMOTION COMBAT (Seaton, folios 4-5): the DPT frame - strength x constitution + 10 x level; the DPG - strength + dexterity + half intelligence; the 10-set turn, the 6-unit set; the three-quarters DPT half-strength line; the five-eighths roll of dexterity for order changes and the return blow, pinned as scanned; the kick rules, the sweep that downs for three units at normal damage, the grab that tells for three units; the recovery ladder - light at 10 DPT, serious at 50, the wish at 150, natural days at half the DPT lost; no challenge to a recovering monk. THE MATRIX (folio 5): the full strike-block-kick grid as printed, CONVERTED to integers - 0 normal, 1 blocked, 2 double, 3 triple, 4 sweep, 5 grab, 6 not applicable - the legend pinned beside the grid, the conversion noted, never silent. HONEST BOUNDARIES: the option replaces the Greyhawk damage system only as a noted variant - the engine's canon damage tables are untouched; the arena is a written-orders minisystem for monk advancement, never core canon; the ceremonial prose (the bows, the arena) rides the provenance. The Fischer box flips this round - the issue-2 report's third flip, 3 closed / 1 open, the systems box closing at the NEXT Dragon round per the R796 pre-flip rule.
